body.html: Who Pacific Park Hotel is right for — to put it as briefly as possible, Pacific Park Hotel Si Racha is a hotel for people who want to stay "right next to everything the city offers" without having to move the car anywhere · It isn't a beachfront resort that lets you wade into the sea out front, and it isn't a small boutique on a quiet lane · It's a 4-star hotel and serviced apartment set inside the Pacific Park mall building — what locals call Sriracha Nakorn — on Srirachanakorn 3 Road, in the heart of Si Racha's business and shopping district, just a few dozen metres from Robinson department store · The clearest selling point is that the moment you step off the lift you can walk straight into Robinson, the supermarket, restaurants and the cinema, with no need to call a car or walk in the sun · It has been open for a long time and has kept up consistently good reviews; it is still open and operating normally, and its Trip.com score sits at 9.1 from 659 reviews · Real reviews line up on who fits here: businesspeople and engineers working in the Eastern industrial zone, Japanese and other expat families posted in Si Racha, and travellers who want a comfortable, central place to stay at an affordable price · Another group who say it's great value are those staying long, a week or a month at a time, because many room types have a kitchenette, a large fridge and a built-in microwave, so daily life works as smoothly as in a real apartment · As for anyone hunting for a luxury beachfront resort with a quiet vibe or wide-open sea views, this place may not be the answer, and you should look toward Bangsaen or Pattaya instead.

Location and getting around — this is unquestionably Pacific Park Hotel's number-one selling point · The hotel sits on Srirachanakorn 3 Road, Si Racha sub-district, as part of the Pacific Park (Sriracha Nakorn) mall building, and is attached to Robinson Si Racha about 50 metres away, while the Pacific Park mall itself is only about 20 metres off · Within walking distance all around you there are supermarkets, restaurants, banks, schools and a hospital, so you barely have to plan everyday travel at all · For sightseers, Koh Loy and the Koh Loy Si Racha bridge, the city's landmark, are a short walk away, and Surasak Montri Park is about 500 metres off · Getting a bit further afield is still easy, because the hotel runs a free shuttle van to Pattaya Beach, Bangsaen Beach, Aeon Mall and J-Park Shopping Center, the spot the Japanese community favours · For people who work here, the hotel is within an easy drive of the Laem Chabang industrial estate and port (about 12 kilometres), and is about 30 kilometres or roughly a 40-minute drive from Pattaya · Si Racha railway station is about 3 kilometres away, and Suvarnabhumi and U-Tapao airports are about 1 hour off · One small note: central Si Racha gets fairly busy with traffic in the evenings, and the hotel's parking is limited when it's crowded, so if you drive yourself you should allow extra time and ask about parking ahead.

"Staying here you hardly need to drive anywhere — take the lift down and you're straight into Robinson and the supermarket, finish dinner in the mall and stroll back to your room easily · The room is spacious with a big fridge and a microwave, so coming to work and staying long is really convenient."

Room types and decor — Pacific Park Hotel has several tiers of rooms to choose from, split between the hotel side (about 380 rooms) and the serviced-apartment side (Residence, about 47 units) · It starts with the Studio at around 30 sqm, the entry room good for short stays, available with either a large bed or two single beds · Stepping up is the Deluxe (including Deluxe Corner) at around 38 sqm, which gives more space, and some are corner rooms with wide windows · And the larger rooms like the One Bedroom Suite at around 60 sqm and the Two Bedroom on the residence side, for families or long-stay guests · What sets Pacific Park apart from the usual city hotel is that many rooms have a kitchenette, a large fridge, a microwave and a toaster, making it easy to cook simple meals yourself and ideal for long stays · Every room has air conditioning that cools well, a flat-screen TV, a work desk, a safe, a balcony, and a private bathroom with a bidet · The decor is a simple, warm-toned business-hotel style, focused on being practical to use rather than flashy · Many reviews agree that the rooms are bigger than the price, very clean, and the beds are comfortable, with housekeeping keeping floors and rooms consistently tidy · For people coming to work or join online meetings, the work desk and stable Wi-Fi also earn praise · The note is that the building and decor lean classic rather than sharply modern, and some spots look like an older-generation hotel in line with the building's age, but in terms of cleanliness and practicality it does well.

Facilities, pool and spa — Pacific Park Hotel has a fairly large set of facilities for a city hotel · The highlight is the outdoor pool with a garden corner and sun loungers, for cooling off after a day of sightseeing or work · There's a gym, a sauna, a steam room and a massage room, a full set for unwinding · On top of that there's a karaoke room, a business centre, coin-operated washing machines and free parking, covering workers, long-stay guests and families alike · The service that really stands out is the free shuttle van to Pattaya, Bangsaen, Aeon and J-Park, which makes getting around much easier for guests without a car · There's a 24-hour front desk, room service, and free Wi-Fi throughout the building · To be honest, from the reviews the pool is the most frequently criticised point, because it's fairly small and in the building's shade almost all day, so the water stays cold and the sun rarely reaches it — especially with kids who come to swim, it can feel too cold · If the pool is your main priority you should set expectations accordingly, but in terms of overall facilities and the shuttle service, it's a lot of value for the price.

Food and bar — the hotel's main restaurant is The Park, which serves Thai and international dishes as all-day dining and is where the breakfast buffet is served · Breakfast is a point that gets quite a lot of praise in real reviews — many say the buffet has plenty of choice, both hot and cold, mixing Thai, Japanese, English and European dishes, which suits the large base of expat and Japanese guests in Si Racha · The freshness and flavour are good for a hotel of this level · There's a bar and drinks service in the restaurant, plus room service to order food up to your room · For other meals the hotel's location helps a lot, because just taking the lift down brings you to restaurants in the Pacific Park mall and Robinson, along with Japanese restaurants, ramen shops and local eateries all over central Si Racha, so many people choose to go out and eat, alternating with dining in the hotel · A note from the reviews is that when it's busy some breakfast items may run out or be slow to refill · Overall, Pacific Park does well on the food front for breakfast, and the rest is helped by the central location that already provides plenty of options all around.

Service — service is another point that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews · Many staff are praised as polite, smiling, friendly and helpful, especially the reception team and the restaurant staff · Housekeeping earns praise for cleanliness and consistently tidy room care, a strength reviews mention often · The free shuttle van and help with calling a car, booking a restaurant or suggesting places to visit also make many guests feel they get more service than they paid for · But to be straight about it, some voices in the reviews note that the front desk's handling of on-the-spot problems in some cases isn't as smooth as it should be, leaving some guests uneasy about how it was dealt with · Overall, service is still a strength and one reason the review scores are high, but the consistency may depend on the time and how crowded it is.

What real reviews say (both praise and criticism) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a central location attached to Robinson and the mall with everything in walking distance, rooms that are spacious and very clean with good housekeeping, many room types with a kitchenette, a large fridge and a microwave that suit long stays, a varied multinational breakfast buffet, polite, smiling, friendly staff, a free shuttle van to Pattaya-Bangsaen-J-Park, and good value for a budget · On the criticism side: the most-talked-about issue is the pool being small and in the building's shade almost all day, so the water is cold and the sun doesn't reach, not great for letting kids swim for long · Next is parking being limited when it's crowded, the front desk's handling of problems in some cases not being smooth, some breakfast items running out or being slow to refill during peak hours, and the surroundings being a small town, so there's some dirt and pollution on the outer roads · Most of these gripes are things you can fix by setting expectations right, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back, which is reflected in the 9.1 score from over 659 real reviews.

"Breakfast is really good, lots to choose from — Thai, Japanese and Western — the staff are lovely and always smiling, and the room is very clean · The only knock is the small pool in the building's shade, the water's a bit cold and the kids couldn't play long; next time I'd still come back for the location and the room more than anything."

Price comparison and value — the Studio's starting price is around THB 1,000/night at normal rates, while the Deluxe and One Bedroom run from about THB 1,300 up to around THB 2,500–3,000 depending on size and season · Compared with other hotels in Si Racha and the Laem Chabang area, Pacific Park feels very good value in terms of location and room space for the price, especially when you factor in rooms that in many types have a kitchenette and a large fridge for long stays, a varied breakfast, and a free shuttle van to Pattaya-Bangsaen-J-Park, a service that isn't easy to find at this price · What makes it even better value is being attached to the mall and Robinson, which saves both time and travel costs in daily life · If you plan to use Si Racha as a work base in the Eastern industrial zone, stay long for a week or a month, or use it as a stopover on the way to Pattaya-Rayong, every baht you spend on this location and convenience pays you back well, in exchange for accepting that the pool and the outer surroundings aren't its strengths.

What to know before you book — there are several things that help your stay go more smoothly · One, if you're staying long or coming as a group, choose a room with a kitchenette and a large fridge such as Deluxe and up or the residence side, which is better value and more convenient than a standard Studio · Two, if you mean to swim or bring kids to the pool, set the expectation that the pool is fairly small and in the building's shade and the water may be cold — go in the late afternoon when the sun reaches it most · Three, if you drive yourself, ask about parking ahead, as it's limited when it's crowded · Four, make the most of the free shuttle van: ask the front desk about the timetable and drop-off points right at check-in, especially if you want to get to Pattaya or J-Park without a car · Five, rooms fill up fast on long weekends and in the high season, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms, and pick free cancellation upfront if your plans aren't set.

Verdict — from all the real reviews, Pacific Park Hotel Si Racha is the hotel best suited to people who want to stay in central Si Racha attached to the mall on an affordable budget, whether you're coming to work in the Eastern industrial zone, staying long for a week, or using it as a stopover on the way to Pattaya-Rayong · A location where you walk down into Robinson and the mall in a single move, rooms that in many types have a kitchenette and a large fridge, a varied breakfast, a free shuttle van, and cleanliness that earns consistent praise make it good value that's hard to match in the area · If you're after a luxury beachfront resort with a pretty all-day pool or wide-open sea views, this place may not be the answer, and you should consider hotels on the Bangsaen or Pattaya side instead · But for a trip where you want central Si Racha comfort at a good price, with clean rooms and friendly service — Pacific Park is a choice that meets that need well, and it's the reason it scored 9.1 from over 659 real reviews.

faq.q: Where is Pacific Park Hotel Si Racha · what can you walk to?
faq.a: The hotel is at 2/1 Srirachanakorn 3 Road, Si Racha sub-district, Si Racha district, Chonburi, part of the Pacific Park (Sriracha Nakorn) mall building in central Si Racha · It is attached to Robinson about 50 metres away and the Pacific Park mall about 20 metres off — take the lift down and you're straight into the supermarket, restaurants and the cinema · Near Surasak Montri Park and Koh Loy Si Racha, close to the Laem Chabang industrial estate and port (~12 km), and about 30 km from Pattaya.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Pacific Park Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,000/night for a Studio of around 30 sqm at normal rates · There are Deluxe and Deluxe Corner at around 38 sqm, a One Bedroom Suite at around 60 sqm with a kitchenette and a large fridge, up to a Two Bedroom on the residence side for families · Many rooms have a kitchenette, a microwave and a toaster, ideal for long stays · You should compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Pacific Park Hotel right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for businesspeople working in the Eastern industrial zone, families and expats posted in Si Racha, and long-stay guests staying a week or a month, because many room types have a kitchenette and a large fridge · It's also handy as a stopover on the way to Pattaya-Rayong · If you're after a luxury beachfront resort with wide-open sea views, the Bangsaen or Pattaya side may suit you better.

faq.q: What pool and facilities does Pacific Park Hotel have?
faq.a: There's an outdoor pool, a gym, a sauna, a steam room and a massage room, plus a karaoke room, a business centre, coin-operated washing machines and free parking · There's a free shuttle van to Pattaya, Bangsaen, Aeon and J-Park · A note from the reviews is that the pool is fairly small and in the building's shade almost all day, so the water is fairly cold.

faq.q: What's breakfast like at Pacific Park Hotel?
faq.a: Breakfast is served buffet-style at The Park restaurant and gets quite a lot of praise in reviews · Many say there's plenty of choice, both hot and cold, mixing Thai, Japanese, English and European dishes, suiting the base of expat guests in Si Racha · The note is that when it's busy some items may run out or be slow to refill.

faq.q: Is Pacific Park Hotel still open · what's its review score?
faq.a: It's still open and operating normally · The latest score is 9.1 from 659 reviews on Trip.com, with many reviews praising the central location attached to the mall, clean rooms, a varied breakfast and friendly staff · The points most often criticised are the small pool in the building's shade and parking being limited when it's crowded, so you should compare several sources before deciding.
